$comment: Ordered SEO fix queue. scripts/seo-daily.mjs opens one Copilot task at a time (in this order) while its check is failing, and closes it once the live site passes. Human tasks are opened alongside. Edit freely: reorder, add, or remove tasks.

tasks.title: Make /optical-object-storage a permanent (308) redirect
tasks.why: A temporary 307 redirect tells Google the old URL may come back, so ranking signals are not consolidated onto /preservation.
steps: Replace `redirect("/preservation")` with `permanentRedirect("/preservation")` from `next/navigation` (check node_modules/next/dist/docs or nextjs.org docs for the Next.js 16 API).
Alternatively add a `permanent: true` redirect in next.config and delete the page — choose whichever keeps the change smallest.

tasks.title: Add a default social share image (og:image / twitter:image) for every page
tasks.why: No page has an og:image, so links shared on LinkedIn, Slack, Teams, and X render without a preview image, which lowers click-through.
steps: Add `app/opengraph-image.tsx` using `ImageResponse` from `next/og` (1200×630) with the Savartus name, the tagline "Manage. Store. Preserve.", and the brand colors already used in the site. Export `alt`, `size`, and `contentType`.
Add `app/twitter-image.tsx` (re-export the same image) so `twitter:image` is emitted.

Confirm the file-convention image is inherited by nested routes (product, insight, and solution pages). If a route defines its own `openGraph` metadata without images, make sure the default image still appears.
Set `twitter.card` to `summary_large_image` in the root metadata if it is not already set.
acceptance: Every page in the sitemap outputs `og:image` and `twitter:image` meta tags that return an image (HTTP 200, image/* content type).

tasks.title: Add Organization and WebSite JSON-LD structured data to the homepage
tasks.why: Organization/WebSite structured data helps Google show the correct brand name, logo, and site name in search results and the knowledge panel.
steps: Render a `<script type="application/ld+json">` on the homepage containing an `@graph` with `Organization` (name Savartus, url https://www.savartus.com, logo using an existing logo file in /public, and contact/sameAs only if those values already exist in the codebase) and `WebSite` (name, url).
Follow the existing JSON-LD pattern in `app/insights/[slug]/page.tsx` (`JSON.stringify(data).replace(/</g, "\\u003c")`).
Do not invent addresses, phone numbers, or social profiles that are not already on the site.
acceptance: The homepage HTML contains valid JSON-LD with `@type` Organization and WebSite.

tasks.title: Put the product category into the homepage title and description
tasks.why: The homepage title "Savartus | Manage. Store. Preserve." contains no searchable category terms, so it cannot rank for searches like "long-term data archive storage".
steps: Change the homepage title to something like "Savartus | Long-Term Data Archive & Preservation Storage" (≤ 65 characters, including the words archive/storage/preservation). Keep the brand first on the homepage only.
Rewrite the homepage meta description to 140–160 characters, summarizing what Savartus offers using only claims already on the page.
acceptance: The homepage `<title>` contains archive, storage, preservation, or lifecycle and is ≤ 65 characters.

tasks.title: Replace generic hub-page titles with descriptive, keyword-bearing titles
tasks.why: Titles like "Products | Savartus" and "Insights | Savartus" waste the most important on-page ranking signal.
steps: Give each page a title with 3+ words that names what it covers. Examples: "Archive Storage Products: ELS Libraries & Software", "Data Archiving Resources & Specifications", "Data Preservation Insights & Articles", "Active Archive Storage Solutions", "Long-Term Data Preservation Solutions".
Keep each full title (including " | Savartus") ≤ 65 characters and unique.
Use only terms that match the content already on each page.
acceptance: Every non-brand page has 3+ words before " | Savartus" and stays ≤ 65 characters.

tasks.title: Shorten page titles longer than 65 characters
tasks.why: Google truncates long titles in results, cutting off the most specific words.
steps: Run `node scripts/seo-audit.mjs --no-psi` to list the pages that are currently too long.

Shorten each title to ≤ 65 characters including " | Savartus", keeping the primary keyword at the front. For Insights, prefer adding a dedicated `seoTitle` field (falling back to `title`) instead of changing the visible article headline.

tasks.title: Rewrite meta descriptions to 70–165 characters
tasks.why: Most meta descriptions are 170–250 characters, so Google truncates or rewrites them. Concise descriptions improve click-through.
steps: Run `node scripts/seo-audit.mjs --no-psi` and open `seo-report/audit.json` to get the failing pages and their current lengths.
Rewrite each description to 120–160 characters: lead with the primary topic, include one concrete benefit, and use only claims already on that page.
For Insights, add an optional `seoDescription` field (falling back to the current excerpt) rather than editing visible copy.
Keep every description unique.
acceptance: Every page's meta description is 70–165 characters and unique.

tasks.title: Add Product JSON-LD to every ELS product page
tasks.why: Product structured data helps Google understand each library model and its specifications. Rich results require offers or reviews, which we deliberately omit because prices are not published.
steps: In `ELSProductDetail`, render `<script type="application/ld+json">` with `@type: Product`, `name`, `description`, `image` (absolute URL), `brand` (`{"@type": "Brand", "name": "Savartus"}`), `category`, and `additionalProperty` entries for key specifications from `data/els-products.ts`.
Do not add offers, prices, ratings, or reviews.
Use the escaping pattern from `app/insights/[slug]/page.tsx`.
acceptance: Every /products/els* page contains valid Product JSON-LD.

tasks.title: Add visible breadcrumbs and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to product and Insight pages
tasks.why: Breadcrumbs replace the raw URL in search results with a readable path and strengthen internal linking to the hub pages.
steps: Create a small reusable `Breadcrumbs` component that renders a visible, accessible breadcrumb trail (`<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`) styled to match the site, plus a matching BreadcrumbList JSON-LD script.
Products: Home › Products › ELS Libraries (/products/els) › <model>. Insights: Home › Insights › <article title>.
Use absolute URLs in the JSON-LD `item` fields.
acceptance: Every /products/els* and /insights/* page contains BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and a visible breadcrumb trail.

tasks.title: Cross-link ELS product models so each is linked from 4+ pages
tasks.why: Some product pages are linked from only 1–2 pages, so Google treats them as low-importance and crawls them less often.
steps: Add a "Compare other ELS models" section to `ELSProductDetail` that links to every other ELS model page with descriptive anchor text (model name plus a short capacity or positioning phrase taken from `data/els-products.ts`).
Make sure /products/els links to every model.
acceptance: Every /products/els* page is linked from at least 4 other pages in the sitemap.

tasks.title: Link every Insight article from 3+ other pages
tasks.why: Several Insights are linked only from the Insights index, so they are hard for Google to discover and receive little internal authority.
steps: Run `node scripts/seo-audit.mjs --no-psi` to list Insights below the threshold.
Extend `relatedArticleSlugs` so every Insight appears as a related article on at least two topically related Insights.
Where a solution or product page discusses the same industry (e.g., medical imaging, government records, media archives, backup), add a contextual "Read the Insight" link to that article.
acceptance: Every /insights/* article is linked from at least 3 other pages in the sitemap.

tasks.title: Expand thin landing pages (homepage, /resources) to 400+ words
tasks.why: The homepage (~300 words) and /resources (~220 words) are too thin to rank for competitive archive-storage searches.
steps: Homepage: add a concise "What Savartus does" section and a short FAQ (3–5 questions) built only from facts already published elsewhere on the site (product pages, Orain, DLM specification, Insights). Link each answer to the relevant page.
/resources: add a 1–2 sentence description to each resource and a short introduction explaining who each resource is for.
Do not invent statistics, customers, certifications, or claims.
acceptance: The homepage and /resources each have 400+ words of main content.

tasks.title: Fix mobile Core Web Vitals on pages below target
tasks.why: Mobile performance is a ranking factor and affects bounce rate.
steps: Open the dashboard or `seo-report/audit.json` (`psi` section) to see which pages miss the targets and by how much.

Typical fixes: give the LCP hero image `priority`/`preload` and correct `sizes`, convert large PNGs to WebP/AVIF via `next/image`, set explicit image dimensions to prevent CLS, and defer non-critical client components and scripts.
Measure before and after with PageSpeed Insights (mobile).
acceptance: Audited pages score ≥ 90 mobile performance with LCP ≤ 2.5 s and CLS ≤ 0.1.

tasks.title: Verify savartus.com in Google Search Console and submit the sitemap
tasks.why: Search Console is the only source of real ranking, click, and indexing data from Google, and it alerts you to penalties and crawl problems.
steps: Go to https://search.google.com/search-console → Add property → **Domain** → `savartus.com`.
Copy the `google-site-verification=…` TXT record and add it at your DNS provider, then click Verify (DNS can take a few minutes to propagate).
Open Sitemaps → submit `https://www.savartus.com/sitemap.xml`.
Close this issue when done. The daily check also detects the DNS record automatically.
acceptance: Property verified and sitemap shows status "Success".

tasks.title: Import the site into Bing Webmaster Tools (also covers DuckDuckGo, Yahoo, ChatGPT search)
tasks.why: Bing's index powers several other search and AI answer engines, and import from Search Console takes about 2 minutes.
steps: Go to https://www.bing.com/webmasters → Sign in → **Import from Google Search Console**.
Confirm the sitemap was imported.
Close this issue when done.
acceptance: savartus.com is verified in Bing Webmaster Tools with the sitemap submitted.
